text: Pioneer 10 launched on March 2, 1972 on a trajectory toward Jupiter and the outer solar system.
Pioneer 10 flew past Jupiter in December 1973, obtaining the first close-up images of Jupiter and its Great Red Spot.
In 1983, Pioneer 10 crossed the orbit of Neptune, then the most distant known planet from the Sun.
NASA's routine science operations with Pioneer 10 ended on March 31, 1997 due to budgetary and power constraints.
Last signal Jan 23, 2003 per NASA Science (a 2003 release says Jan 22).
safe_text: NASA Science records the last signal received on January 23, 2003 (a 2003 press release cited January 22).

text: Pioneer 10 was powered by SNAP-19 radioisotope thermoelectric generators, whose electrical output gradually decayed below transmitter thresholds.
